name: fx

surfaces.label: `fx` in a terminal: the interactive Zig TUI (also `fx resume [last|<id>]`, `fx -c`, `fx -r`, `--resume-<id>`). One native binary, installed by https://fx.sh/setup.sh to ~/.local/bin/fx (or $FX_INSTALL_DIR); no app bundle, no bundle id, no interpreter. argv[0] is `fx` when run by name, so only `names` can match: path_contains cannot work for the by-name case, and the name is shared with antonmedv/fx, the Go JSON viewer (brew formula `fx`), which this row will also match. The only discriminator the probe cannot use is the store: a real agent pid appears in ~/.fx/sessions/<id>/owner.live. On macOS fx re-executes its own binary by absolute path as short-lived helpers, so they match this row too and are vetoed by exact argument: `fx __fx_foreground_session__ <deadline> <cmd...>` (every foreground shell tool call; the command's shell is its child, so a shell is NOT a direct child of the session), and `fx --fx-internal-terminal-host|-launcher|-control|-tmux-launcher|-tmux-capture` (background command host, shared, stays 30 s after its last session). exclude_args also vetoes management subcommands by exact argument; a directory or prompt word equal to one (`fx --add-dir workspace`) would be vetoed. `ask` and `acp` have their own surfaces below. `pr` and `issue` run one model turn and exit; they are excluded and not tracked. A new session's id is generated (12-char base64url) and is NOT in argv; only resume forms carry one, so map pid to session through owner.live (pid) or lsof on session.lock, never through argv. session_id_args reads `resume <id>` and `--resume <id>`; the probe cannot read the fused `--resume-<id>` form (it tests `flag value` and `flag=value` only), and `resume last` yields the word `last`, which has no store file. Not matched by design: `fx session resume <id>` is an interactive resume too but `session` is in exclude_args (it also covers the read-only `fx session <id> --json`), so that one form is a false negative. On upgrade (ctrl+g) fx replaces its own process in place (std.process.replace, same pid) with `<installed fx> resume <id> --upgrade-relaunch [<rev>]`, so the row still matches and the id is in argv; inferred from src/core/app/app_entry_runtime.zig, not seen live.

`fx ask "<prompt>"` (noninteractive one-shot; also `printf ... | fx ask`, `fx ask --resume <id|last>`, `--json`, `--no-save`). Alive means working; it exits at the end of the request (exit 130 on interrupt). args_contain is a SUBSTRING test, so an interactive `fx --add-dir ~/tasks` would also match here and score higher than the TUI surface (misfiled as always working); accepted because interactive launches rarely carry path arguments. Sessions are saved unless --no-save.

`fx acp`: Agent Client Protocol server on stdin/stdout, spawned by an editor with the configured absolute path to fx (`{"command":"/absolute/path/to/fx","args":["acp"]}`), one process per project, one session and one prompt at a time, newline-delimited JSON-RPC. The parent is the editor, not a terminal. Sessions are created over JSON-RPC (session/new, session/load), so no session id is in argv. Hooks and Herdr reporting fire only for interactive scope, not ACP. Substring args_contain, same hazard as the ask surface.

working_signals.meaning: events.jsonl in the session directory is an append-only log of frames {schema_version, seq, timestamp_ms, event:{<variant>:{...}}} with variants user, assistant, tool_call, tool_result, steering, turn_completed, interrupted, context_checkpoint. The exact turn signal is an OPEN TURN: the last frame is not turn_completed or interrupted (source state machine nextConversationTurnOpen: user opens, turn_completed or interrupted closes). Keep it working only while the pid in owner.live is alive. The probe cannot read frame types, so it only raises on a fresh write. Write granularity during a long model call or tool call is not known.
fallback; a guess, never measured. fx holds no sleep assertion and spawns no caffeinate, so there is no level signal.

waiting_signals.meaning: internal lifecycle hook fired after a user decision prompt becomes active (approval prompt in ask mode, ask_user_question, route recovery). NOT user-configurable: only built-in providers register handlers (Herdr and notification sounds). Nothing outside the process can subscribe.

when launched inside Herdr, fx reports idle, working or blocked to Herdr over a short-lived Unix socket, with custom status permission, question or recovery for blocked; source `custom:fx`. Interactive scope only; disable with FX_HERDR=0. Read state from Herdr, not from fx.

waiting_signals.name: afplay
waiting_signals.meaning: short-lived direct child `/usr/bin/afplay $TMPDIR/fx-<cue>.m4a` (cue files fx-success.m4a, fx-error.m4a, fx-bloom.m4a, fx-press.m4a, fx-release.m4a, fx-toggle.m4a, fx-click.caf). Turn end (success or error cue) and attention required (success cue) are the only cues that mean done or waiting; both default on for macOS (notifications.turn_end, notifications.attention_required). The other cues are not turn signals: bloom at startup, press on cancel (escape), click after /model or /fast changes, all gated by the sound switch; release and toggle only at sound level max (notifications.max, default false). So an afplay child can appear at startup, on cancel or during typing-adjacent UI actions without any turn ending. It is absent when sound is off. Attention also writes a BEL to the terminal. Never count afplay as a tool child and never as working.

hooks.config: none. Lifecycle hooks exist only as an in-process Zig runtime (src/core/hooks); no settings key, no docs page, no external command hook. Handlers are registered by built-in providers only.

telemetry.how: none. https://fx.sh/docs/using-fx/data-and-privacy says fx sends no product telemetry or usage analytics; no OTEL or OTLP string in src. Local diagnostics only: FX_TRACE=1 / FX_TRACE_LOG (trace), FX_DEBUG_RECORD=1 / FX_RECORD (terminal recordings under ~/.fx/recordings/), ~/.fx/usage.jsonl (fx usage).

notes: Read from official docs (fx.sh/llms-full.txt) and the public source at main (Sep 30 2026, v0.0.12); nothing was seen running, so every CPU floor and window is a guess. Best exact signal is the open-turn record in events.jsonl gated by a live pid from owner.live, which the probe cannot read; until it can, a fresh events.jsonl write raises working and CPU is the fallback. Do not expect a shell tool child: on macOS the direct child of a working session is `fx __fx_foreground_session__ ...` (same executable name as its parent), the shell is a grandchild, so tool_children is left out. Waiting comes from Herdr's socket report or the internal AttentionRequired hook (not subscribable), and afplay is a done-or-waiting chime, not a working signal. Match by name only (argv[0] is `fx` by name) and expect antonmedv/fx to match; confirm with a pid hit in ~/.fx/sessions/*/owner.live. `fx pr` and `fx issue` are not tracked. The libfx Node and WebAssembly embeds run inside a host app and create no fx process. Adversarial pass 2026-09-30: sound cues corrected (afplay also fires at startup, on cancel and after /model or /fast, so it is a weak done-or-waiting hint, not a clean one). Known false positives: antonmedv/fx and any `fx <file|expr>` invocation, plus `fx wat` (exits at once). Known false negatives: `fx --add-dir workspace` and other flag values equal to an excluded word, and `fx session resume <id>`. Known misfile: a path or model containing the substring `ask` or `acp` is scored as the ask or ACP surface. Upgrade relaunch keeps the pid (execve-style replace), so no duplicate row.
